$comment: The mandatory sandbox controls the platform requires before it will authorize any execution. This file is the single source of truth for a set that two modules must agree on and that neither may import from the other: services/runner produces the assessment and holds container-runtime access, and apps/api consumes it and is build-guarded against ever depending on that module. Each side has a test asserting its own set equals this file, so adding a control to the gate without teaching the control plane about it, or the reverse, fails the build instead of silently widening or narrowing what 'all mandatory controls passed' means.
$controlsComment: The mandatory set is SCOPED TO THE SECURITY PROFILE VERSION, which is derived from the container runtime. It is not one list any more because the two runtimes do not make the same controls observable: gVisor's guest exposes no NoNewPrivs line in /proc/self/status, so a check that reads the flag can say nothing there, while the same runtime makes host-kernel syscall mediation demonstrable and the baseline cannot. Keeping one shared list would have forced a choice between demanding evidence a runtime cannot produce and dropping a control the other runtime can prove -- either way a control name would stop meaning what it says. Exact equality still applies WITHIN each version, in both directions, so an assessment produced under one profile can never satisfy the other.
$egressComment: Controls required ONLY before an ALLOWLIST execution is authorized. They are a separate set from the mandatory controls above because they are required under a different condition: every execution needs the mandatory ones, and demanding these of a DENY_ALL run would make a sandbox that wants no network depend on the egress subsystem being healthy. Within their own scope the same exact-equality rule applies on both sides.
